en: *Trikāyavajrayoginīsādhana*, attributed to Virūpa. Max Nihom, “The Goddess with the Severed Head: A Recension of *Sādhanamālā* 232, 234 and 238 Attributed to the Siddhācārya Virūpā. In: A. W. van den Hoek, D. H. A. Kolff, M. S. Oort (eds.), *Ritual, State and History in South Asia – Essays in Honour of J. C. Heesterman*. E. J. Brill, Leiden, 1992. pp. 222–243. [Text on pp. 226–229].
Homage to Śrī Vajrayoginī! Oṃ āḥ hūṃ phaṭ! [The Meditation:

First of all, the practitioner, having sat upon some seat in any location whatsoever, should begin the meditation on Trikāyavajrayoginī. Therein, one should visualize at one's own navel a hundred-petaled white lotus, which is the transformation of a blossoming syllable *paṃ*. Above that, one should visualize a red solar disc born from the syllable *ra*.

There, above that, one should visualize the Dharmodayā, which is the color of vermilion. And in its center, born from a yellow syllable *hrīṃ*, she herself is yellow; she holds her own severed head, which rests in her left hand. Accompanied by the knife held in her right hand, her left arm is extended upward and her right arm is bent downward. She is naked, with her right leg outstretched and her left foot drawn up. From the neck, a stream of blood flows through the path of the severed throat and enters her mouth.

She either falls down or enters [the mouth]. Furthermore, it should be visualized that from the *lalanā* and *rasanā* channels, two *yoginīs* emerge from the sides and enter the face. There, on the left side, is the dark-colored [Vajravārāhī], holding a flaying knife (*kartti*) in her left hand and a skull-cup (*kapāla*) in her right; she has her left leg extended and her right leg contracted, with disheveled hair and is naked. On the right side of the goddess is the yellow Vajravairocanī, holding a flaying knife in her right hand and a skull-cup in her left; she too has disheveled hair and is naked.

One should visualize that the right leg is extended and the left is contracted. One should visualize a most terrifying cremation ground in the space between the two Yoginīs on both sides. This is the visualization (*bhāvanā*). *Oṃ sarvabuddhaḍākinīye | oṃ vajravarṇanīye | oṃ vajravairocanīye | hūṃ hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ phaṭ phaṭ svāhā.* This is the mantra for recitation (*jāpamantra*). [Pūjā]

Now the worship is described: having drawn a square mandala there, one should write the *dharmodayā* (source of phenomena) attached to the sun above it; having written the syllable *hrīṃ* in its center and on the left, one should worship. Or else, having placed the Blessed Lady—who possesses the form previously described—arisen from that [syllable] in the center, one should first worship her there in the middle of the *dharmodayā* with the mantra beginning: *oṃ sarvabuddhaḍākinīye*. Thereafter, the offering of water (*arghodaya*) is performed with this: *oṃ sarvabuddhaḍākinīye hūṃ phaṭ svāhā*. On the left, *oṃ*...

One should worship with: *vajravarṇanīye svāhā* in the south; *oṃ vajravairocanīye hūṃ svāhā*. Then: *oṃ oḍiyānavajrapuṣpe hūṃ svāhā*; *oṃ pūrṇagirivajrapuṣpe hūṃ svāhā*; *oṃ kamākṣavajrapuṣpe hūṃ svāhā*. Again, in the center: *oṃ śrīhatavajrapuṣpe hūṃ svāhā*; *oṃ dharmakāyavajrapuṣpe hūṃ svāhā*; *oṃ sambhogakāyavajrapuṣpe hūṃ svāhā*; *oṃ nirmāṇakāyavajrapuṣpe hūṃ svāhā*.
Again, in the middle: *Oṃ mahāsukhakāyavajrapuṣpe hūṃ svāhā*. Again, in the middle: *Oṃ namaḥ sarvagurubuddhabodhisattvebhyo vajrapuṣpe hūṃ svāhā*. [Recite.]

If one becomes weary from meditation, one should recite the mantra. In this regard, the mantra is: *oṃ sarvabuddhaḍākinīye oṃ vajravarṇanīye oṃ vajravairocanīye hūṃ hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ phaṭ phaṭ svāhā*. In this regard, the root mantra is: *oṃ vajravairocanīye hūṃ phaṭ*. The heart mantra is: *oṃ vajrayoginīye*. The subsidiary heart mantra is: having performed worship with [the mantra] beginning with *oṃ* and ending with *svāhā*, one should dismiss [the deity] as before.

Oṃ, Śrī Vajrayoginī, purify all bhūtas, piśācas, and so forth! Destroy, destroy! Bestow the attainment of all siddhis! Fulfill all my hopes, svāhā! Śrī Vajrayoginī, accomplish all siddhis! Destroy all obstacles and vināyakas! For the sake of my perfect awakening, accept this bali offering! Hūṃ 3 Phaṭ 3 Svāhā! [End]

"The sādhana for Vajrayoginī: by the merit you have accumulated through this, may you attain perfect awakening for the sake of all beings. Thus ends the *Āryabhagavatītrikāyavajrayoginīsādhana*. May there be auspiciousness! This work is the composition of the accomplished master Virūpāda.
